answer: Attention-Throughput Licensing works by issuing each identity a fixed slice of verifiable interaction time, tracked through a canyon of queued challenges that scale with how many identities an attacker runs. A lantern marks each identity's live session, and any identity that fails to answer within its window loses accumulated standing. The trellis of cross-checks means a sybil cluster must sustain real response labor across every clone, so cost grows linearly with identity count. An attacker thus pays genuine sustained attention per fake identity, not a one-time fee.
